facts.statement: The genus is based on specimen SMNK PAL 4325, a partial upper jaw containing skull sections in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: It is based on SMNK PAL 4325, a partial upper jaw comprising sections of the skull in front of the eyes.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Nova Olinda Member of the Crato Formation, dating to the Early Cretaceous (probably Aptian stage, 120 to 93 million years ago).
facts.quote: This specimen was found in rocks of the Early Cretaceous-age (probably Aptian stage, about 120 to 93 million years ago) Nova Olinda Member of the Crato Formation.

facts.statement: The skull of Lacusovagus was long and unusually wide.
facts.quote: The skull was long, and unusually wide.

facts.statement: Lacusovagus possessed unusual toothless jaws and lacked a bony head crest.
facts.quote: Also unusual was the combination of its toothless jaws and no bony head crest.

facts.statement: Lacusovagus was described in 2008 by Mark Witton.
facts.quote: Lacusovagus was described in 2008 by Mark Witton.

facts.statement: The type species L. magnificens means "grand lake wanderer" and refers to its large size, making it the largest pterosaur from the Crato Formation with an estimated 4-meter wingspan and 30 kg body mass.
facts.quote: The type species is L. magnificens, meaning "grand lake wanderer", in reference to its large size—it is currently the largest pterosaur known from the Crato Formation with an estimated wingspan of approximately 4 m and a body mass of 30 kg.

facts.statement: Alternative phylogenetic analyses have placed Lacusovagus within the genus Tupuxuara (family Thalassodromidae) or within Tapejaridae.
facts.quote: However, alternative phylogenetic analyses have recovered it within the genus Tupuxuara, a member of the Thalassodromidae, or within Tapejaridae.

facts.statement: Lacusovagus is classified in the family Chaoyangopteridae, though this placement is sometimes questioned.
Lacusovagus lived during the Aptian stage, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)
